title: HPC, AI and ML Infrastructure Essentials
subject: HPC/AI/ML
description: What high-performance computing, AI, and machine learning need from infrastructure, how to qualify these workloads, and how to avoid overpromising.

lessons.title: What HPC, AI, and ML workloads need
lessons.body:
High-performance computing (HPC) runs large calculations by combining many processors in a cluster. AI and machine learning (ML) training is often similar: it needs many parallel processors, usually graphics processing units (GPUs), and large volumes of data.

The main infrastructure needs are:

- **Compute:** many CPUs or GPUs, connected closely enough to share work.
- **Memory and storage:** fast storage that can feed data to the processors without delay.
- **Network:** high-speed, low-latency links between nodes.
- **Power and cooling:** dense racks draw and generate a lot of heat.

A design that is strong on compute but weak on storage or networking will run slowly.

lessons.title: Training and inference
lessons.body:
AI work has two phases:

- **Training:** the model learns from data. This is compute-heavy and often runs for hours or days.
- **Inference:** the trained model is used to make predictions. It needs less compute per request but must respond quickly and reliably.

Buy-or-build decisions depend on which phase the customer needs. Many customers start with inference on an existing model rather than training their own.

lessons.title: Qualifying an AI or HPC opportunity
lessons.body:
Before proposing hardware, ask:

- What problem should the workload solve, and how will success be measured?
- What data is available, where is it stored, and how clean is it?
- Is the workload training, inference, simulation, or analytics?
- What are the performance targets and the time limit for results?
- Who will run and maintain the environment, and what skills exist today?
- What are the power, cooling, and rack space constraints?

If the answers are unclear, propose a short assessment or proof of concept before a large purchase.

lessons.title: Avoiding overpromising
lessons.body:
AI projects often fail because expectations are unrealistic. Do not promise specific model accuracy or speed-up figures without a benchmark on the customer's own workload. Be clear about:

- Which parts of the solution are standard and which need customisation.
- The skills and time needed to build and operate the solution.
- The ongoing costs of power, cooling, support, and upgrades.

An honest scope builds trust. A pilot that meets a clear target is a stronger outcome than a large purchase that does not.
